messages:
sara: FYI customer AcmeCorp opened an urgent ticket — they see auth failures and 502s followed by cross-region responses. They assert requests should stay in us-west-2 (account pinned). Ticket INC-4602. Example request id: req_02HXA3LZ

michael: looking at logs now. I can see bursts of 401s then 502s from the us-west-2 pool around 2024-11-05T09:07:32Z. Shortly after, traffic gets routed to eu-west-1 and the responses include x-redwood-region: eu-west-1. Might be healthcheck marking nodes unhealthy then fallback. Ping @josh and @luis.

opsbot: [alert] heartbeat-missed \u2014 pool: us-west-2-auth, window: 2m, missed_heartbeats: 4, last_heartbeat: 2024-11-05T09:06:30Z

tania: customer provided a trace showing initial 401s from our auth service then a 502: 

```
> GET /v1/query HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< x-service: auth-service-usw2
< x-request-id: req_02HXA3LZ
\n... a few retries ...

< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< x-redwood-region: eu-west-1
< x-request-id: req_02HXA3LZ
```

sara: they reported ~8 minutes of intermittent failures. Customer is upset because they pay for regional isolation. Need fast mitigation and clear RCA.

josh: quick recap from infra side: we recently adjusted the heartbeat window for auth-service to 15s (down from 30s) to detect real failures faster. That makes the heartbeat system more sensitive to transient GC pauses or auth cache rebuilds. Looks like an auth cache rebuild caused short auth errors, heartbeats missed, and routing flipped.

luis: adding logs: the auth-service process in one instance hit a 12s stop-the-world GC while rebuilding caches after a config reload. Heartbeat missed during that pause. The routing layer then considered the instance unhealthy and started diverting traffic. We also saw retries that attempted other regions.

anita: critical question: should account-level region pin override automatic global fallback? customer expects pin to be respected except during full region outage. Current behavior: automatic fallback has priority for availability. That policy needs revisiting for enterprise accounts.

michael: mitigation we did: 1) temporarily excluded pinned enterprise accounts from automatic fallback (applied 2024-11-05T09:18Z) 2) rolled heartbeat sensitivity back to 30s for auth-service 3) killed the noisy instance and warmed a fresh one. Metrics show requests for AcmeCorp returned to us-west-2 at 09:20:05Z.

opsbot: [deploy] routing-config v3.2.1 -> hotfix-3.2.0-enterprise-pin applied by michael at 2024-11-05T09:18:47Z

sara: customers asks for reproducible steps to understand the failure. Keep repro non-invasive. Suggested safe repro: call the API repeatedly while we trigger an auth cache reload on one auth node in the us-west-2 pool (we will coordinate and do it in our lab). Example client loop:

```
for i in {1..120}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" -H "X-Redwood-Request-Id: repro-$i" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/status | jq .; sleep 0.5; done
```

Internal command to simulate (lab only):

```
# on auth server
systemctl reload redwood-auth && sleep 2 && sudo -u redwood ./auth-cache-rebuild --quiet
```

josh: long term fixes: 1) add heartbeat hysteresis (require sustained misses across distinct instances before region marked unhealthy) 2) separate auth-service heartbeat from routing heartbeat (service-level vs pool-level) 3) implement enterprise pin cooldown: only failover pinned accounts if >30% of pool capacity is unhealthy for >5m 4) audit config reloads to avoid simultaneous cache rebuilds.

luis: I'll draft the config change PR for heartbeat hysteresis and a new metric (rapid-region-switch rate) to alert on flip-flops.

anita: product note: update SLA language and support runbook to clarify when we will override region pin for availability vs when we respect pin.

sara: please own the customer update. Outline: what happened, immediate mitigation (hotfix + rollback), repro steps (lab-only), and timeline for permanent fixes. Also include compensation options if they want (credit).

michael: I'll attach timing graphs and auth-service GC traces to the incident ticket.

josh: I'll include the changelog and PR links. Will also add canary gating for future heartbeat sensitivity changes.

opsbot: [note] incident INC-4602 mitigated at 2024-11-05T09:21:10Z

sara: thanks everyone. We should convert this to a postmortem and publish in #incidents once reviewed. Closing loop with AcmeCorp first. :thumbsup:
